A1.justification: Both complete 22-page PDFs describe EgoMono4D and contain readable text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices. Renamed baselines and relocated sections can be matched reliably.

before.justification: V3 reports original reconstruction and scene-flow evaluations, model ablations, robustness tests, timing measurements, and depth/pose results in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: V4 retains these original empirical results and adds evaluations of CUT3R in existing comparisons.

M1.justification: The UniDepth backbone, video adaptors, confidence decoder, camera-pose alignment, training losses, and sliding-window inference remain unchanged. Renaming MFVR+UniDepth does not alter the proposed method.

E1.justification: Training retains H2O, HOI4D, FPHA, EgoPAT3D, and Epic-Kitchen. Evaluation retains HOI4D, H2O, POV-Surgery, and ARCTIC-HOI, with the same reconstruction, scene-flow, depth/pose tasks and temporal test scenarios.

E2.justification: CUT3R is added to reconstruction comparisons in Table 1, scene-flow comparisons in Table 5, camera-pose comparisons in Table 8, and the speed comparison. MFVR+UniDepth is retained as Modularized Version; existing comparators remain.

E3.justification: Dataset splits, sample counts, preprocessing, training budgets, evaluation clips, metrics, and alignment procedures are retained. The relocated speed evaluation still uses 40-frame videos, one RTX3090 GPU, and batch size 1.

E4.justification: The model/loss ablations, FPS sensitivity, window/overlap tests, and HOI-region analysis retain their settings and evidence in Tables 2, 3, 6, and 7. Qualitative comparisons and failure cases are also retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run or seed counts, confidence intervals, significance tests, or comparable statistical uncertainty estimates. V4 introduces no new uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: V4 adds CUT3R results while retaining matched pre-existing values. For example, CUT3R has POV-Surgery reconstruction CD 107.6 mm and scene-flow ADE 304.6 mm in Tables 1 and 5. Its newly reported 0.115 seconds/frame is faster than EgoMono4D's unchanged 0.218, moving EgoMono4D from second to third in the timing comparison.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions and derivations, including Equations 1–17 for reconstruction, alignment, losses, inference, and evaluation metrics, are retained. No new assumptions, proofs, or theoretical results appear.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: unified, self-supervised, fast and generalizable egocentric 4D reconstruction with strong reconstruction performance. The added comparator supplies evidence without redefining these core claims.

C2.justification: Appendix E newly interprets CUT3R's speed advantage as a very small difference outweighed by reconstruction quality. Appendix G expands the existing discussion of joint consistency versus individual depth/pose accuracy. Previously documented failure conditions and limitations remain.

D1.justification: Implementation details, hyperparameters, hardware, data processing, and metric implementation information are retained. Timing settings are relocated, and the existing project URL and code/model availability statement remain equivalent.

R1.justification: Section 2 and the bibliography retain the same 104 works and research positioning. CUT3R was already discussed in v3, and the depth-estimation works cited in v4's expanded discussion were already cited; the novelty framing remains unchanged.

P1.justification: V4 renames MFVR+UniDepth, moves the speed subsection into Appendix E, updates appendix references, and expands local discussion. It also revises affiliations, adds acknowledgments, and corrects several typos. Most prose and the overall narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: Tables 1, 5, and 8 gain CUT3R rows and reorder the modularized baseline. The speed chart gains a CUT3R bar and moves from main-text Figure 5 to appendix Figure 10. Other illustrations are retained with local placement, numbering, and caption changes.

improvement.justification: Adding the previously discussed CUT3R improves comparative completeness: Tables 1 and 5 support EgoMono4D's reconstruction advantage, while Table 8 and Figure 10 expose CUT3R's better pose estimates and faster inference. This is a limited gain with the method and previous evidence unchanged. Appendix E understates the timing tradeoff by calling 0.115 versus 0.218 seconds/frame a very small difference, but the additional evidence still makes the comparison more informative.
